name: Maison Vaudoise
tagline: Everyday knitwear made from fibres we can name.
description: A Lausanne ready-to-wear label building a compact permanent collection instead of seasonal drops. Every garment ships with the full list of mills that touched it, which is why the sourcing team spends more time in spinning halls than in showrooms.
mission: Prove that a small European label can publish its entire supply chain without losing margin.
vision: A wardrobe where every piece can be traced back to the field it grew in.
goals: Move the full jersey range to traceable organic cotton by 2027
Reduce the number of tier-2 suppliers from 14 to 6
Publish a verified chain for every product page

name: Atlas Cotton Collective
tagline: Aegean organic cotton, ginned within 40 km of the field.
description: A growers' cooperative of 340 smallholder farms across the Aegean basin, running its own ginning facility so lot identity survives from field to bale. Bales carry a field code that downstream spinners can resolve back to a specific harvest block.
mission: Keep organic cotton smallholders economically viable through direct mill relationships.
vision: Cotton sold by field name, not by grade alone.
goals: Extend drip irrigation to 80% of member farms
Reach full bale-level digital identity by 2027
seeking: Brands willing to contract multi-year volumes

name: Filatura Brescia
tagline: Ring-spun yarns with lot identity kept intact.
description: Third-generation spinning mill running ring and compact lines for fine-count cotton and cotton-linen blends. Refuses to blend incoming bales across origins, which costs throughput but keeps every cone attributable to a single grower lot.
mission: Spin traceable yarn without hiding origin behind a blend.
vision: A European spinning sector where lot identity is the default, not a premium service.
goals: Convert the remaining two open-end lines to compact spinning
Run the mill on 100% contracted hydro power
seeking: Organic cotton growers with lot-level data
Weavers and knitters in Western Europe

name: Tessitura Lario
tagline: Narrow-width weaving and circular knitting on the same roof.
description: A Como mill that kept both its air-jet weaving hall and a circular knitting floor when most of the valley specialised. Useful for brands that want shirting and jersey from a single greige source with matching yarn lots.
mission: Give small collections access to mill-grade fabric without mill-grade minimums.
vision: Short runs treated with the same rigour as bulk.
goals: Cut greige stock by half through made-to-order scheduling
Add a fourth knitting line for fine-gauge jersey

name: Teinturerie des Vosges
description: A dyehouse and finishing plant that rebuilt its effluent line into a closed loop in 2019, recovering 78% of process water. Runs reactive and natural dye programmes side by side, with full recipe archives per lot.
mission: Take the water question off the table for European textile finishing.
vision: Dyeing that returns cleaner water than it takes.
goals: Reach 90% water recovery by 2028
Phase out the last two conventional dye classes
seeking: Weavers and knitters in Western Europe

name: Confecções Douro
tagline: Small European runs, without the small-run penalty.
description: A Porto cut-make-trim factory organised in eight independent cells rather than one long line, which is what lets it accept 150-piece orders alongside 20,000-piece programmes. Runs its own pattern and sampling room.
mission: Keep European garment making viable for labels that do not order by the container.
vision: Factory access decoupled from order size.
goals: Bring average sampling turnaround under 10 days
Train 40 new machinists through the in-house school by 2027
seeking: Emerging brands in DACH and Nordics

name: Lino Baltico
tagline: Dew-retted Baltic flax, scutched on site.
description: Grows and processes flax on 2,400 hectares of Lithuanian farmland, handling dew retting and scutching in house. Sells long line fibre to European spinners and tow to insulation manufacturers, so nothing leaves the site as waste.
mission: Rebuild a Northern European linen chain that does not detour through Asia.
vision: Flax processed within a day's drive of where it grows.
goals: Add a hackling line to sell combed sliver directly
Supply flax tow to three insulation manufacturers by 2027

name: Refibra Ibérica
tagline: Mechanical recycling that keeps staple length usable.
description: Takes post-industrial cutting waste and post-consumer garments, sorts them by colour and composition, and tears them back to fibre without re-dyeing. Output is sold as colour-sorted recycled cotton, which spinners can blend without a dye step.
mission: Make recycled cotton good enough that nobody has to justify using it.
vision: Cutting-room waste treated as inventory, not disposal cost.
goals: Reach 40% post-consumer input by 2027
Push average staple length above 22 mm

name: Nordwolle Handel
tagline: European wool and speciality fibre, traded with paperwork that holds up.
description: A Bremen trading house sourcing wool from Northern European flocks and speciality fibres from certified growers. Its value is documentation: every lot arrives with scouring records, origin declarations and test certificates already assembled.
mission: Remove the documentation gap between growers and mills.
vision: Fibre trading where provenance travels with the bale by default.
goals: Digitise the full lot archive back to 2015
Add three certified European wool scourers to the network
seeking: Spinners in Southern and Western Europe
Wool growers in the Nordics and British Isles

name: Atelier Romand Construction
tagline: Buildings specified by material passport, not by catalogue.
description: A Fribourg design-build practice working on public and residential projects in Romandie. Every project ships with a material passport listing origin and end-of-life route for each component, which forces the sourcing team upstream of the usual merchant layer.
mission: Build so that the next generation can take the building apart and reuse it.
vision: Material passports as standard practice on every Swiss tender.
goals: Reach 60% reused or recycled material by mass on new projects
Source 80% of structural timber within 300 km

name: Holz Emmental
tagline: Structural timber traced to the forest parcel.
description: Sawmill and timber merchant working exclusively with Emmental and Entlebuch forestry cooperatives. Each delivery carries the forest parcel identifier, felling season and drying record, so contractors can put real data in a material passport.
mission: Keep Swiss structural timber in Swiss buildings, with the paper trail to prove it.
vision: Timber sold by parcel, like wine is sold by plot.
goals: Add a CLT pressing line by 2028
Cover 100% of volume with parcel-level identifiers

name: Granulat Jura
tagline: Limestone aggregate and a quarry with a closure plan.
description: Operates two Jura limestone quarries and a washing plant, supplying graded aggregate to concrete producers within a 60 km radius. Both sites run under a restoration plan agreed with the canton before the first blast.
mission: Extract the minimum needed, as close as possible to where it is poured.
vision: Quarries that leave usable landscape behind.
goals: Supply 30% of volume as washed recycled aggregate by 2028
Complete restoration of the north site by 2030

name: BetonCycle Rhein
tagline: Structural concrete with demolition rubble as the aggregate.
description: Takes demolition rubble from the Basel-Freiburg corridor, processes it into certified recycled aggregate, and casts it into structural precast elements. Publishes a declared recycled-content percentage per batch rather than per product line.
mission: Turn the region's demolition waste into its next load-bearing structure.
vision: Recycled aggregate as the default specification, not the exception.
goals: Raise average recycled aggregate content from 45% to 65%
Certify a low-clinker binder for structural use by 2027

name: Metallwerk Schwaben
tagline: Electric-arc steel, cut and formed for building envelopes.
description: Processes scrap-based electric-arc furnace steel and recycled aluminium into structural profiles, rebar and facade substructures. Every coil carries a melt certificate, which is what lets contractors declare recycled content honestly.
mission: Supply building steel whose carbon figure survives scrutiny.
vision: Recycled metal specified by number, not by adjective.
goals: Move all forming lines to contracted renewable power by 2027
Publish EPDs for the full profile catalogue

name: Vitrum Alpes
tagline: Triple glazing built around a demountable frame.
description: Manufactures insulating glass units and structural glazing for Alpine climates, using a demountable spacer system so units can be opened, reglazed and resealed instead of scrapped. Roughly a third of input cullet comes from its own take-back stream.
mission: End the assumption that a failed glazing unit is landfill.
goals: Take back 5,000 units per year for reglazing by 2028
Reach 50% recycled cullet in standard units
seeking: Design-build practices in the Alpine arc

name: Isolana Verde
tagline: Insulation batts from flax tow and wood fibre.
description: Makes bio-based insulation from agricultural by-products that would otherwise be burned — flax tow, hemp shives and sawmill wood fibre. Boards are bound without formaldehyde and are compostable at end of life.
mission: Insulate buildings with what farming and sawmilling already produce.
vision: Bio-based insulation priced against mineral wool, not above it.
goals: Open a second line for wood fibre boards in 2027
Source 100% of fibre within 800 km
